findings.summary: The margin note that reports the bounding surface is drawn in the reference grey #929292 at fontsize 13, which measures 3.1:1 against the white background on all four delivered panels. That is below the 4.5:1 a reader needs for text at this size; it is legible here, but it is the quietest text on the page while it carries the only statement of the surface's vertex count and class margin, so a reader scanning the panel can miss it. Darkening the note to the legend's own text colour would fix it without changing what the note says or where it sits. The measured ink: grey note glyphs are #929292 (594-625 px per panel), the legend text is #1f1f1f at 16.5:1 and the axis note #cc0000 at 5.9:1.

The delivered rasters are 735x657 px (frame 137) and 766x657 px (frames 144, 179, 44) against the 14x7.2 in 1400 px house canvas the script asks for, because savefig runs with bbox_inches='tight' around a portrait poloidal drawing whose legend and note float to the right. Below the note row (y > 330) the region x > 340 is blank in every panel, and the poloidal drawing itself occupies only the left ~44 percent of the delivered width. Nothing is lost at the delivered size and the six rubric items pass, but the composition is a portrait panel with a floating legend rather than the declared slide canvas, so the four panels do not read as the house layout beside other figures.

The solved axis marker, its coordinate annotation and the leader joining them are drawn in #cc0000, and the solved X-point shares that red. Nova's figure rules keep red for a limit being broken, so on these panels red names neither a limit nor a failure while the terminal state they mark is the figure's subject. The marks are legible and unambiguous against the grey reference set, and the legend names each one, so this does not impede reading; it is a colour-role deviation a reader of the repository's other figures will notice. A highlight hue from that style's role set, or the near-black used for limits, would carry the same emphasis without borrowing the limit colour.

Frame 137's caption cites two distances for what a reader will read as one object: 'its recorded boundary 0.329 m from the wall' and, two sentences later, 'Its eight-vertex bounding surface comes within 0.006 m of the limiter'. The panel's own margin note reports only the vertex count and the class margin (-0.021), so neither number can be reconciled against the picture, and 0.329 m and 0.006 m differ by a factor of fifty for two things both called a boundary. They are in fact the flux boundary's nearest approach to the wall and the host ring's gap to the limiter; naming the two objects distinctly in the caption would let the reader see which is which.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: No caption merely repeats a title: the panels carry no on-canvas title, identity is in the file name, and each caption adds the terminal residual (0.0624, 5.93, 0.0273, 0.197) and a topology or boundary statement. Frame 44's caption states that its recorded X-point lies outside the drawn field and that the panel therefore carries no mark or legend entry for it, which the raster confirms at seven legend entries. The one caption finding recorded above is a clarity defect in frame 137's distance statements, not a repeated title.
item_verdicts.prior_repairs: The three blocking findings of the previous figure review at head a3cd2debc are verified repaired in these renders: the axis annotation now sits in the margin under the panel with a leader and no contour pixel inside its bounding box (it was drawn straight through the flux field); the bounding surface is drawn as a grey solid eight-vertex ring with its count and class margin noted (it was absent and silently dropped); and both null sets are drawn, with the EFIT X-point visible as a grey hollow cross in all four panels (it was never plotted). The carried non-blocking composition finding remains open and is restated above.
item_verdicts.verdict_basis: Every verdict was read from the attached PNGs at their delivered sizes. No verdict is derived from SVG text, glyph coordinates or markup.
